body:
STORY-1350 needs requeueing, and the fact that I cannot do it is STORY-1353's second live instance today

STORY-1350 shelved with RequestChanges. PR 1974 is open and CI-green at 3ff9d789; the drain correctly moved on to BUG-1234 and will not re-drive it. Round-2 rework brief is already on the spec, and both findings are confirmed — I checked each against origin/story-1350-work before writing, rather than relaying the verdict.

  Criterion 3: generate_review_prompt in aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs builds its output from the requirement title plus extract_acceptance_section. It never touches the spec's comments, so there is no path by which the implementer's approach statement reaches the reviewer. Round 1 therefore cannot compare stated intent against the diff, which is the whole point of writing the statement down.
  Criterion 7: Step 3d of aida-pickup.md tells every pickup to post. Its only skip is on the headless variable being unset, which is the interactive case, not the no-parseable-acceptance case your rule adds.
  Criteria 1, 2, 6 verified. Criteria 4 and 5 are not-applicable by your binding scope decision, and I said so explicitly in the brief so nobody implements the advisor preview or the 20-spec measurement you removed.
  One thing I added: both ends key on the `## Implementer approach` marker, so it should be one shared constant rather than a literal in each place. A marker that drifts breaks the loop with no test failing anywhere.

THE ASK: `aida queue add STORY-1350 --for implementer --user role:implementer`, so the next wave picks it up.

WHY I AM ASKING. That command refuses for me: "queuing work for execution needs advisor authority (advisor role or an interactive session)". The spec is already Approved — by you — already routed to implementer, already groomed with execution_mode drain, and already driven once by this wave. Putting an approved spec back on the queue after a review round decides nothing; the disposition happened when you approved it. But the substrate classifies it as disposition, so it stops at your gate.

That is the second time today. The first was TASK-168, where the status reset genuinely IS yours and asking was right. This one is different in kind and identical in treatment, which is exactly the conflation STORY-1353 names. It is queued in the current wave; here are two concrete instances for its acceptance, if useful:

  - Requeue an Approved, already-routed spec after a RequestChanges round. Refused. No disposition is being made; the same spec goes back to the same queue for the same role.
  - The workaround available to me is AIDA_SESSION_ROLE=advisor, which is worse than the refusal, because it makes an audit trail say the advisor queued it. A seat that has to impersonate another seat to do its own job produces a false record, and that record is what the ledger EPIC-69 is building would read.

I am not using that workaround. The operator was explicit that the product seat is an independent proxy-human perspective and not a seat granted advisor authority, and quietly assuming the role to unblock myself would hollow out the distinction he asked for. The round trip costs a few minutes and you have been answering in less.

Wave otherwise healthy: BUG-1234 in phase 1, sixteen still queued, no other shelves.
